rationale: While comparative muscle MRI studies between distal hereditary motor neuropathies (dHMN) and distal myopathies (DM) confirm that a distal-to-proximal gradient of fat replacement and an early reticular pattern of fat infiltration are significantly characteristic of neurogenic motor neuropathies (present in ~80% of dHMN and absent or rare in typical distal myopathies, which more frequently display a moth-eaten or confluent pattern), conflicting evidence exists in general neuromuscular radiology literature reporting reticulated/honeycomb infiltration patterns in certain distal myopathy subtypes. Furthermore, the provided literature lacks specific validation cohorts for the rare dHMN11 subtype (SPTAN1-related dHMN), preventing complete generalization.

evidence.text: In a cohort comparing 78 patients with distal myopathies and 31 with dHMN, a length-dependent pattern with a distal-to-proximal gradient of fat replacement was significantly more common in dHMN, and a reticular pattern of fat infiltration was exclusive to dHMN patients, whereas moth-eaten patterns predominated in distal myopathies.

source.title: Muscle MRI contributes to the differential diagnosis between distal myopathies and distal hereditary motor neuropathies
source.quote: A length-dependent pattern of muscle involvement, a distal to proximal gradient of fat replacement along the length of the muscles and severe and widespread involvement of foot muscles were more common in patients with dHMNs... A reticular pattern of fat infiltration was exclusive to patients with dHMNs, while the moth-eaten pattern predominated in DMs.

evidence.text: In a study of 84 patients with suspected genetic dHMN, muscle MRI revealed predominant distal lower leg fat replacement in 97.6% (82/84) and a characteristic reticular pattern of fatty replacement progressing to muscle islands in 79.8% of individuals.

source.title: Muscle magnetic resonance imaging of a large cohort of distal hereditary motor neuropathies reveals characteristic features useful for diagnosis
source.quote: Fat replacement was predominant in the distal lower leg muscles (82/84 cases)... We observed a reticular pattern of fatty replacement progressing towards what is commonly known as 'muscle islands' in 79.8%.

evidence.text: In neuromuscular imaging review, inherited distal myopathies and related muscular disorders can themselves demonstrate heterogeneous reticulated or honeycomb fatty infiltration patterns, challenging the claim that reticular patterns are strictly exclusive to neurogenic disorders.

evidence.text: Comparison of neurogenic (CMT1A) and myogenic (DM1) disease using 3D radiomic texture analysis on quantitative muscle MRI confirmed that neurogenic neuropathy exhibits significantly steeper disto-proximal fat fraction gradients and higher entropy/contrast reflecting reticular fat replacement compared to confluent myogenic infiltration.

source.title: 3D Radiomic Texture Analysis of Quantitative Muscle MRI Enhances the Distinction Between Myotonic Dystrophy Type 1 and Charcot–Marie‐Tooth Neuropathy Type 1A
source.quote: CMT1A targeted the anterolateral compartment with significantly steeper disto-proximal fat gradients (p < 0.05). TA revealed higher entropy and contrast, and lower homogeneity in CMT1A compared to DM1, reflecting a more reticular pattern of fat infiltration vs. the confluent pattern in DM1.

conflicts: While Payá et al. found reticular fatty infiltration to be exclusive to dHMN compared to distal myopathies, broader radiological classifications (Tai et al., 2025) describe reticulated/honeycomb patterns occurring in specific myopathic phenotypes.
No prospective MRI series exists isolating SPTAN1-specific dHMN11 patients; existing dHMN imaging series are largely aggregated across diverse genetic etiologies (e.g., BICD2, HSPB1, DYNC1H1).

new_directions.question_text: Does SPTAN1-associated dHMN11 specifically exhibit the classic distal-to-proximal reticular pattern on lower limb muscle MRI seen in other dHMN subtypes?
new_directions.rationale: dHMN is genetically heterogeneous, and while aggregate cohorts demonstrate ~80% reticular fat infiltration, individual genetic subtypes can display atypical or proximal-predominant distributions.

new_directions.question_text: Can 3D radiomic texture metrics (entropy and contrast) reliably discriminate distal myopathies with reticulated/honeycomb appearance from dHMN reticular patterns?
new_directions.rationale: Subjective visual assessment may confuse reticular neurogenic changes with honeycomb myopathic changes, whereas quantitative radiomics may provide objective thresholds.
